Manchester City legend Kevin De Bruyne insisted that any potential punishment for breaching financial rules will not change what Pep Guardiola’s team achieved and their memories of success.

The Belgian was a key pillar during the spell of unprecedented domestic dominance and has a statue commissioned outside the Etihad Stadium.

De Bruyne is back in town with Napoli for Tuesday’s Champions League tie, reiterating his ‘love’ for City and its owners, while revealing recent talks with chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak.

The 35-year-old brushed off suggestions that silverware collected during his decade at City would be tarnished if the club lost their appeal and were sanctioned after being found guilty of the vast majority of charges levelled at them.

De Bruyne’s trophy haul – six Premier League titles, one Champions League, two FA Cups and five Carabao Cups – were largely secured outside of the nine-year period in which City were scrutinised, up to 2018.

Sources indicate that ‘I’m proud of what I've done as a football player,’ De Bruyne stated. ‘Honestly, this is my club, I love the owners. I've talked about a lot of stuff outside football (with them), I've even spoken to Khaldoon about how to buy a club and everything.

The 36-year-old brushed off suggestions that silverware collected during his decade at City would be tarnished if the club lost their appeal.

Industry observers note that ‘It (stripping of titles) still doesn't change (anything), my football has not changed. I don't think a lot of people will change in their mind how they view me as a player, or how we played.

Recent findings suggest that ‘But everybody has his own opinion and other people may be disgraced a bit. I can't change anything about that.’.

De Bruyne’s final two seasons at City were plagued by injury before he joined Napoli on a free transfer in 2025 and his first return in last year’s Champions League lasted just 26 minutes as he hobbled off.

Classed as the greatest player in the club’s modern history, De Bruyne was typically forthright on the uncertainty surrounding his former employers after the guilty verdicts read by a three-person independent commission.

‘My feelings have never been different,’ he added. ‘Honestly, the way that I feel is just the way that I've been treated by this club, what I've done with this club for me personally, and how we've worked together as a group.

‘Of course, it's a lot of things that have been going on. I have nothing but affection for this club, and that will never change. Even now, the people who treated me and my family for 10 years is the most notable thing.’.

De Bruyne left City under duress, vehemently disagreeing with the club’s decision not to offer him a latest contract following a spate of injuries before choosing Napoli – and his long-term future in Serie A is now appearing in doubt.

According to recent reports, all eyes in Italy were on the midfielder’s public response to an interview published with his wife, Michele, in which she was reported to have criticised life in Naples and yearned for a move away. Those comments were taken out of context, according to a visibly frustrated De Bruyne, with PSV Eindhoven looking at securing a transfer in January.

De Bruyne left City under duress but revealed recent talks with chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak.

But City supporters will have been more interested in how far De Bruyne went in backing their club ahead of next month’s appeal hearing.

‘In life there are rules, but everybody plays to the limit, I would say,’ he claimed, seemingly referring to how financial rules are interpreted by the Premier League’s elite clubs.

‘I played in between the white lines, and I competed with other players, and I had many experiences with my teams.

‘So for me that's the thing that I value most. The most important thing is the relationships between everybody that I had and how you manage these things, and I've given my all.’.

De Bruyne smirked as he discussed how he knew exactly how City would attack Napoli given his knowledge of the club and manager Enzo Maresca, who was Guardiola’s assistant during the 2023 Treble campaign.

Maresca is facing criticism after three defeats and a draw in their last four league games. The Italian called for calm over recent performances and believes that the transition from Guardiola was always going to represent a bumpy road.

‘It's like a reset, a restart, after 10 years with the same manager, same face, same words, same method,’ Maresca remarked.

It has been revealed that ‘It's not easy to all of a sudden change. For me personally, it's all normal, and hopefully as soon as possible we can find the right balance in all the lines - defensive, midfield - and we can be consistent, which for me is the difference between us and other clubs.’.

Più squadre di Serie C, sfide secche e diritti TV: ecco le due ipotesi allo studio per il futuro della Coppa Italia.

In a recent development, la Coppa Italia potrebbe cambiare volto nelle prossime tre stagioni. Nel nuovo bando per i diritti audiovisivi pubblicato dalla Lega Serie A, con scadenza al 14 dicembre, compaiono infatti due diverse formule pensate per rilanciare un torneo spesso snobbato fino alle fasi finali. A scegliere quale adottare sarà il mercato televisivo: prevarrà il format legato all'offerta economica più alta ricevuta dai broadcaster, con il via libera dell'Assemblea.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Sources indicate that la prima opzione, il Format "A", conferma l'impianto attuale della competizione con 44 squadre al via. Prevede solo 4 club di Serie C nel turno preliminare e l'ingresso delle prime otto classificate della passata Serie A direttamente dagli ottavi di finale con il vantaggio di giocare in casa. Sul piano economico, la Lega ha fissato una richiesta minima di 54 milioni di euro a stagione, pari a 162 milioni complessivi nel triennio. Una soluzione già collaudata che mantiene stabile la struttura del torneo e il relativo valore d'asta per le emittenti interessate.

Il Format "B" allargherebbe il torneo a 56 squadre, portando a 16 i club di Serie C con priorità alle Seconde Squadre (Under 23) di Serie A. Tutte partirebbero subito tranne le prime otto di Serie A (dai sedicesimi), con 24 sfide secche al primo turno, possibili incroci immediati tra A e C e l'ipotesi del sorteggio per il fattore campo. Anche le semifinali sarebbero in gara secca, aggiungendo un turno senza aumentare le gare per le finaliste, mentre le Under 23 non potrebbero affrontare le rispettive Prime Squadre se non in finale. Qui la base d'asta sale a 61 milioni annui (183 milioni nel triennio), trasformando il format in una leva commerciale per i broadcaster.

The Netherlands came crashing down to earth after hammering Greece as they were outclassed and outmuscled by Germany in Berlin.

Oranje went into the final match of the Nations League group stage with high hopes of recording their first win over their old rivals in seven matches stretching back to 2019.

Instead they suffered their second worst defeat ever at the hands of Germany, but still progressed to the knockout stages thanks to their thumping 7-0 win in Amsterdam on Friday.

Coach Xavi Hernandez was forced to make one change in midfield as Jurriën Timber replaced Barcelona’s Frenkie de Jong, who pulled out with an obturator muscle strain.

Germany shaded the first half and went ahead five minutes before the break when Freiburg striker Derry Scherhant cut in from the left hand side and beat Bart Verbruggen with a curling strike into the top corner.

Scherhant had struck the post minutes earlier, while the Dutch might have taken the lead earlier when Crysencio Summerville slipped in the penalty area as he tried to control a cross by Cody Gakpo.

Sources indicate that but in the second half the Dutch fell apart. In the 60th minute Florian Wirtz shoved Denzel Dumfries off the ball and had space to tee up a left-footed shot from the edge of the area that gave Verbruggen no chance.

Nico Schlotterbeck added a third from a free-kick five minutes later, before Wirtz drifted past Gakpo on the right side of the penalty area to score his second.

The humiliation was complete when Brajan Gruda capped a fine attacking performance by firing in a rebound.

Sources indicate that dumfries made no excuses afterwards for what he admitted was a “terrible performance”. “We gave the ball away too easily, left too much space and were too weak in the challenges,” he told NOS. “We can’t let that happen.”.

By LEWIS BROWNING, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 16:03 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 16:05 EST, 23 November 2026.

Former Manchester United midfielder Paul Scholes has become the latest ex-Red Devil to tear into the club's defence, criticising Leny Yoro following his red card in his side's 4-0 defeat by Liverpool.

Yoro was sent off less than eight minutes into United's clash with their rivals at Anfield on Sunday, tripping Alexander Isak as he ran in on goal after an error from Matthijs de Ligt.

He has had a mixed time of things since his £52million move to Old Trafford in 2024, though has been playing in a leaky United defence that has conceded 23 goals in 11 Premier League matches this season – with only Crystal Palace conceding more.

Several different members of United's defence have come under fire this season, and, on Monday, it was the turn of Yoro.

'The Premier League at this minute just looks a little bit too much for him,' Scholes said on The Good, The Bad and The Football, sponsored by Midnite.

Recent findings suggest that he added: 'You know what, he’s come in to a really bad setup defensively now. I think they also made the point yesterday if he went in next to (Virgil) Van Dijk he might look a little bit better but he doesn’t look Premier League level. He looks like a rabbit in the headlights.'.

Paul Scholes (pictured) has suggested Leny Yoro is not yet ready for the Premier League.

Yoro was sent off in the opening minutes of Manchester United's 4-0 defeat by Liverpool.

It has been revealed that fellow former United midfielder Nicky Butt, who played alongside Scholes for United between 1994 and 2004, added: 'If that’s Man United in our day, he’s on loan like a Jonny Evans or a John O’Shea. He’s a great talent that will come good.'.

Scholes, though, wasn't having any of it.

According to recent reports, he replied: 'I’m not sure how much of a great talent he is. I think he has shown a little bit of a sign in the France squad but every time I’ve seen him he doesn’t look at the races. Everything’s happening around him and he’s just a bit, oh, what do I do?'.

United have also faced criticism for their apparent lack of running this season, with eyebrows raised when Youri Tielemans mentioned in the summer that they didn't do much prior to the campaign getting under way.

The club rank 17th for distance covered in the top flight this season, with Liverpool, Brentford and Everton below them. The latter two will almost certainly pass them though after their game on Monday.

That, according to Butt, is down to the players.

According to recent reports, 'We’ve had our say about the players and they’re just not good enough,' he stated. 'It is the most unathletic team I’ve ever seen in Man United.

Sources indicate that 'I’m going to go through a team and I’m trying to be as honest as I can. Forget the quality for right now. For me, physicality-wise, if you go through a team, the right back, he’s physically OK, but he’s not amazing. De Ligt or Harry, whoever he’s going to play in there, physically not great. Martinez for me is physically not great. You got Yoro who will physically come good.

Nicky Butt (pictured), meanwhile, has criticised the physical ability of many of United's players.

In a recent development, 'Then I go on to the midfield, none of them are physically good enough. Kobbie can get about the pitch 15-20 yards, but he’s not box to box. Noted that numerous times. He’s got a lot of talent. He’s got a lot of things going for him. I think he’s a top player. He ain’t got the legs. He needs to have legs around him but his legs around him at the minute are Bruno and Tielemans - and they can’t run around.

'Look at Mbeumo, I think he’s OK but he’s not going to blow anybody away. I think Cunha can run. So then you look at the whole squad and you’re saying three players can run.

'What I’m getting at there, and it sounds like I’m being a draconian but what you have to do first and foremost when you go to Anfield is to be able to compete physically and they can’t so they have no chance.'.

Ajax moved into a clear second place in the Eredivisie with a routine 3-0 win against ADO Den Haag, as Feyenood slipped to fifth after losing to local rivals Excelsior.

Davy Klaassen took just three minutes to stroke home the opening goal for Ajax and added a second just before half-time.

By then ADO had been reduced to 10 men following the dismissal of Matteo Waem for hauling down Tolu Arakodare.

But there was a blow for Ajax ahead of next weekend’s visit to Feyenoord when Jorthy Mokio, scorer of the second goal, was taken off injured after an accidental collision with Sékou Sylla.

Feyenoord, who started the month top of the Eredivisie, suffered their first home defeat in the derby against Excelsior since 1980 to continue a slump in form that has seen them draw two and lose four of their last six games.

Givairo Read’s blistering shot gave Feyenoord the lead after just two minutes, but Excelsior were ahead by half-time and made it 3-1 when Casper Windell headed in a corner after 58 minutes. Despite an own goal by Jan Plug, on loan from Feyenoord, Excelsior were not to be denied.

PSV remain a point clear of Ajax at the top of the table after they cruised to a 4-1 win at NEC, with Filip Kostic opening the scoring with his first goal for PSV and his first Eredivisie goal since 2014, when he was playing for Groningen.

Utrecht sacked their managed Anthony Correia after just 14 matches after sinking to 15th place in the table with a 3-2 home defeat to Cambuur.

Correia won just four games after leaving Telstar, the club he led to promotion two seasons ago and where he spent his entire 15-year playing career. Youth team coach Mark Otten will take charge of the first team while Utrecht search for a replacement.

Willem II, searching for their first Eredivisie win in 30 matches, took a shock lead away to Twente despite being reduced to 10 men in the first half when Devin Haen was given space in the area to shoot past Joël Drommel.

The home side struggled to turn their superiority into goals, but an equaliser by Ramiz Zerrouki and a late header by Marko Pjaca gave them the points they needed to rise to third place above Feyenoord.

AZ also overtook Feyenoord as they beat Sparta 5-1 with a dominant second-half display, while Fortuna Sittard kept in touch with the leading group with a typically gritty 1-0 win at Go Ahead Eagles.

Go Ahead Eagles 0-1 Fortuna Sittard.

Sparta Rotterdam 1-5 AZ Alkmaar.

Twente Enschede 2-1 Willem II Tilburg.

It has been revealed that L'ancien Vert, Mathys Saban opère désormais au Mâcon 71 (N2), après un passage au Luxembourg (Titus Petange, Racing FC Union). Au sortir d’une crise interne marquée par une grève de l’entraînement, Mâcon 71 jouait un match key sur le terrain de la réserve d'Annecy. À dix contre onze (après l'exclusion de l'ancien Vert, Israël Kinunga) et après avoir été rattrapé sur penalty, les Mâconnais ont montré qu’ils savaient réagir. C'est Mathys Saban, entré en jeu à la 71ème, qui a donné la victoire (1-2) aux siens, à la toute dernière minute du match. Un autre ancien Vert, Yoann Greco est entré en jeu à la 65ème.Avec 11 points, Mäcon 71 pointe à la 7ème place, à 8 points du leader Bourgoin dans le championnat de N2.

In a recent development, mathys Saban (24 ans), joueur offensif polyvalent, est arrivé au centre de Formation de l'ASSE en 2017, en provenance de l'US Torcy qui a fourni aux Verts Lamine Ghezali, Alexandre Valbon, Josué Gago et Marwan Nzuzi, Lucas Gourna-Douath, Mathis Amougou, Fodé Camara, Axel Dodote. Il a gravi toutes les étapes de la formation et signé son premier contrat pro de 3 ans avec l'ASSE le 5 juin 2020, contrat qui sera prolongé de 2 ans en février 2023.En 2020-2021, il joue son premier match en pro, le 23 mai 2021, 12 minutes lors de ASSE-Dijon : 0-1.En 2021-2022, il participe à 3 matchs de Ligue 1 : - 21 août 2021, 21 minutes : ASSE-LOSC : 1-1- 28 août 2021 : 19 minutes : OM-ASSE : 3-1- 12 septembre 2021 : 30 minutes : Montpellier-ASSE : 2-0En 2022-2023, il participe à 3 matchs de Ligue 2 qui se soldent par 3 défaites, et 1 match en Coupe de France : - le 29 octobre 2022, Coupe de France, 30 minutes : ASSE-Rodez : 0-0 (3-4 tab)- le 7 novembre 2022, 45 minutes, Metz-ASSE : 3-2- le 12 novembre 2022, 17 minutes : ASSE-Rodez : 0-2  - le 26 décembre 2022, 33 minutes : Annecy-ASSE : 2-1.

Industry observers note that le 31 août 2023, il est prêté au club luxembourgeois de l'Union Titus Petange pour la saison 2023-2024. Victime d’une rupture du tendon d’achille au début du printemps 2024 lors de son prêt à l’Union Titus Pétange, Mathys Saban revient à l'ASSE pour la saison 2024-2025 mais ne joue que 77 minutes en N3 pour sa 8ème et dernière saison sous le maillot vert. Il retourne  dans le Grand-Duché durant l'été 2025 (au Racing Football Club Union Lëtzebuerg), et inscrit en septembre 2025 son premier but en L1 luxembourgeoise. Malheureusement son contrat est rompu début 2026 et, après 6 mois sans club, il rejoint donc le Mâcon 71 qui a raté de peu l'accession au Championnat National, devancé par Hauts Lyonnais.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways

  • That was the question of the day, and each of the four guests were asked to discuss various aspects of the debate from financial fairplay to club takeovers by foreign entities to racism.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Yesterday evening, Selecao correspondent Nathan Motz accepted a unique opportunity to appear as a guest on the Moral Maze – a BBC radio broadcast dealing with matters of moral and ethical significance.

Is football a moral force for good? That was the question of the day, and each of the four guests were asked to discuss various aspects of the debate from financial fairplay to club takeovers by foreign entities to racism.

Nathan’s segment was concerned with whether football has transcendent moral value, and what that is exactly. Is there a greater significance to the game we are watching, or is it merely 22 humans kicking a leather ball into a net?

Join Nathan as he elaborates on the most significant takeaways of what was a fascinating discussion on the sport and morality in general.

Industry observers note that football, for some, may be the most poignant reminder of the moral universe in which we live. While debate has raged for centuries regarding the precise origin of moral absolutes and how humans ought to live, it is simply unavoidable to say humanity is often troubled by events surrounding the game we all love so dearly.

In not so distant history, every normal act of human life would have been assigned some degree of moral significance. Every action had inherently moral indicators - for good or for evil. Today, postmodern views of morality dominate. These describe morality as an entirely subjective dimension. In other words, it cannot be pinned down exactly whether behaviors are objectively good or bad. We can only find fault with someone else’s interpretation based on their own unique moral code. Morality is relative to the individual or society.

Industry observers note that yet last night’s dialogue concerning football and human behavior was filled with moral accusations and claims which strongly suggested humans are not content with relativist morality. Indeed, we are at times frightened by and disgusted with what we observe in and around football. Our sense of moral justice is deeply disturbed. But with respect to what exactly?

It has been revealed that in responding to the panelist’s questions, I observed a familiar paradigm. Each time I have discussed any aspect of moral behavior, the speculation humans are good or at worst morally neutral animals continually reemerges. This widely accepted presupposition is then followed shortly by disgust at some aspect of human behavior. Almost as if to ask “why are all these good humans behaving so badly?” while ignoring the very real implications of this line of inquiry. A question rendered unanswerable by the insistent a priori assumptions from which it was derived.

If humans are intrinsically beneficent, conscientious, fair, humble, and honest then why is football rife with racism, misogyny, greed, disenfranchisement, lies, cheating, violence, and the hypocrisy to deny the occurrence of any such behaviors except when a rival club is the guilty party? Behaviors which are perpetrated by individual supporters, fanatical groups, club administrations, corporate bodies such as FIFA, political entities, nations, and even the players themselves. No one participating faction is guiltless.

To so blithely sidestep more sufficient explanations for the empirical reality of wickedness in football and in human behavior more generally is not just factually incorrect. It undermines real attempts to understand the root of these behaviors where they might be dealt with more effectively.

To listen to The Moral Maze episode entitled “Football: a moral force for good?” produced by BBC radio and featuring PortuGOAL’s Seleção correspondent Nathan Motz click on this link.

Industry observers note that furthermore, in good faith, how successful is a response against heinous evil when those perpetrating it are regarded as behaving in accord with their unique moral ambitions? Humans refuse to accept their indisputably objective moral lacking at a fundamental level. This restricts us from ever doing any more than “stamping out” the alleged impropriety of others – while we ourselves may readily engage in these very same behaviors. Moral relativism cannot account for the moral outrage emanating from all corners of the football world. Is Qatar wrong to perpetrate human rights atrocities or is it allowable because their culture is indifferent? Is hooliganism objectively wrong, or only when someone else’s club is responsible?

In a recent development, the overlooking of our own failings while lashing out at others for theirs is quintessential to the morally fallen nature of humanity itself. Football tells all. There are not good people and bad people. There are only people who both willfully and unintentionally transgress the moral code embedded in each of our hearts. A moral law which can only have ever been given by a moral Lawgiver. Otherwise, it is truly your word against mine as it pertains to the moral validity of all behaviors - even those which may deeply violate your conscience.

Football generates an episodic, semantic, and imagistic description of universal archetypes: good and evil, sacrifice and greed, cruelty and mercy, hero and anti-hero. It speaks to every arc of life’s plotline: tragedy, comedy, victory, defeat, the finite nature of our circumstances. It is one of the preeminent existential dialects alongside religion, visual art, written and spoken language, music, and theatre. Football plucks a primal chord.

As metaphysics have been curtailed to just physics in the modern secular West, football has only elevated our awareness of the often dire moral predicaments of our species. Yet it is clear the moral conversation does not originate on a football pitch. The pitch is but a grand stage upon which moral themes may be observed and critiqued, a mirror held in front of our own soul.

Recent findings suggest that the desire for ultimate purpose, for meaning beyond the material realm, never disappeared in modernity. Arguably, it has only become more desperate as the outcry for ultimate significance comes under more scrutiny and criticism by those who constrain ontological explanations to those accounted for by physics. The severity of the mental health crisis in the West is in no small part explained by the terrifying existential awareness we are cut adrift in an abstract sea of meaningless, hopeless wandering between two oblivions - that before mortal life began and that at mortal life’s end. Let football be one voice which reassures you - there is ultimate meaning and good reasons why football so unsettles our craving for justice.

In a recent development, in a palpable, unavoidable way, football and supporter communities across Europe are encountering moral quandaries. In Portugal, age-old debates between FC Porto and Benfica have routinely been haunted by, in many cases, farcical and cynical hypocrisy. Throughout its history, the FPF has been susceptible to showing partiality to a club, player, or style which ultimately degrades the performance of our beloved Seleção. Deny it all we like, and not one aspect of this reality is changed.

Sources indicate that in conclusion, whatever your thoughts or beliefs on the subject of moral significance, its origin, the meaning of life, and how football draws that out, I hope it will be beneficial to examine these matters more deeply. In my zeal, I admit I have not always been prudent to initiate these discussions in a way which respects thoughtful disagreement. It is my hope this effort to bring that discussion to Portuguese football will be well-received and carefully pondered. But I will contentedly listen to those followers who may be genuinely unhappy or unsupportive of this or any other idea about which I write.

The readers of this website and the larger Portuguese football loving world are my people. It is a joy and a responsibility I take seriously whenever I have the opportunity to raise vital questions about the Selecao, the game, and our lives in general.

Tottenham Hotspur have never before in the club’s history begun a league season without scoring a single goal in the first four games, although having done so after spending £329m on new players really does take some doing.

“Please score a goal!” was the homemade sign from two Spurs fans upon which the television cameras lingered at the end of the game, although the jaunty felt-tip design and glued-on team crest were rather upbeat compared to the gloom of the stadium. Spurs have tried to outrun their past but it just keeps catching up with them.

Sources indicate that A team reimagined, a manager freshly launched and yet they are back in the same grip of anxiety that accompanied them on two consecutive 17th-place finishes in the last two seasons. By the end of this they might have been glad to escape with a single point against Everton, the one team in the Premier League who closed the window with a net transfer profit.

Recent findings suggest that for Roberto De Zerbi, there was another passionate defence of his team afterwards. “The people, the fans already understand if I make excuses or not,” he said. “I came last season when the s--- was like this”, he gestured to a level somewhere around the midpoint of his forehead. “I have always been… not positive but realistic. I am sorry for the result that it’s not immediately the improvement. We played as a team. We didn’t score. We didn’t win [but] we played as a team.”.

Indeed he co-opted the Italian term “sbloccare” to describe his team’s problem. They simply need to unlock – or unblock – the team and the goals would flow. He joked that in Italy he would be lauded for two consecutive clean sheets in this game and the previous one against Nottingham Forest. “What did you write?” he demanded of one of the Italian newspaper correspondents. “You have the passport.”.

Spurs have one last game at home this month, on Saturday against Aston Villa, to end the streak in September. They were into the second half before the first attempt on target that obliged Jordan Pickford to make a save – Mateus Fernandes’s shot slapping limply against the Everton goalkeeper’s gloves to ironic cheers from the home fans.

At the end De Zerbi could not contain his frustration, unable to wait until he reached the privacy of the dressing room to tell Mathys Tel where he had gone wrong. He did so with the Spurs substitute still wiping the sweat from his brow on the pitch. The player did not look at all impressed. De Zerbi remarked later that he was simply reminding his player of what it took to play as a central striker.

“There is a term in Italian, ‘sbloccare’ that literally translates as ‘unblock’… I know we can score goals and win games. We have to respect the history of the players – if you forget [Dominic] Solanke and [Omar] Marmoush the others haven’t scored many in their careers. I think we can find the goals with the quality of the players.”.

It has been revealed that spurs play Liverpool at Anfield in the Carabao Cup on Tuesday before Villa a week today. The Spurs record at home is dismal. In the last 35 games they have won just five, drawn 10 and lost a remarkable 20. This upcoming stadium has become a problem for the team in it – or maybe it is the other way around.

Sources indicate that A good result for Everton, who were under pressure for most of the first half but had much the better of it after the break. David Moyes’s team finished the game with more shots on target than the home team. Moyes managed the game well and trusted his team to withstand the Spurs possession in the first half until they reached a point where Everton could start to push back.

Hard to pick out any major chances – it was that kind of game – but Brennan Johnson should have won it for the away team in the second half. The ball was cut back to him by Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall and the former Spurs man skied his shot.

Industry observers note that some surprised faces then when Moyes stated later that he had expected a lot more from his team. He acknowledged the resilience in defence and the importance of the clean sheet. “We played well enough,” he said, “but when we had the ball we turned it over more often than we should have done.”.

The game had started with Vitaliy Mykolenko being tortured by the pace of Sávio and ended with the Ukrainian left-back being given the man of the match award. Like many of his team-mates, he had hung in there. There was another fine performance from Jarrad Branthwaite at centre-half and Moyes noted that he hoped it might earn him a place in the England squad. “He is still finding his way back from injury,” Moyes said, “it would be great if he could get a call-up.”.

In the directors’ box were the usual pained expressions of Vinai Venkatesham, the Spurs chief executive, and chairman Peter Charrington. They sat alongside Vivienne Lewis, daughter of the patriarch Joe. There is a certain fatigue about the home crowd when faced with afternoons like this which suggests they have seen so much that the bar is quite high – or low – to provoke a really splenetic response. Perhaps it is just too early in the season although the final whistle was met with boos.

The first shot on target of the entire game for either side was a free-kick struck by James Garner in added time at the end of the first half. Spurs had started at a ferocious pace although they could not sustain it.

De Zerbi complained about the pre-season injuries on tour in Australia and also the lack of time he had to integrate Sávio and Marmoush. He said that his team were not in the right “physical condition”.

Sources indicate that “We played very well in the first 30 minutes and maybe the energy and the fact we didn’t score – we lost confidence.” By the end, he had sent on James Maddison, Tel, Lucas Bergvall and Mohammed Kudus to little avail. Everton looked more likely to win it.

Speaking to Sky Sports, the Everton defender said: “You look at the game from the start, they put us under pressure and we had to dig deep to stay in the game. Then we grew into the game towards the end of the first half and highlighted that mentality again in the second half.

In a recent development, “We had chances to win the game as well. The backs to the wall mentality will help us go a long way. If we can keep clean sheets, you can go a long way in the league. But it’s not just us the defenders. It’s the whole team working hard. It’s a team effort.”.

Brennan Johnson spent two years at Tottenham and scored the winning goal in the 1-0 Europa League final victory over Manchester United in May 2025, ending the club’s 17-year trophy drought.

After a short, disappointing spell at Crystal Palace, Johnson joined Everton last month, with Dwight McNeil moving in the opposite direction.

Midfielder took exception to negativity surrounding club after moves for players on deadline day failed to materialise.

“We signed Jack [Grealish], which was nice, and I’d been speaking to him,” says Dewsbury-Hall, sitting in a café at the club’s Finch Farm training base. “But I had seen all the stuff [online], all the meltdowns about this and that and, in all honestly, it annoyed me a bit.

“I get where people are coming from. Everyone wants to sign everyone and have the perfect squad, but there are still 19 lads in this building who are going to hopefully take this club to good things this year. That was getting disregarded. I was seeing people saying: ‘We’ll be lucky to stay up this year.’.

According to recent reports, “What message is that sending to the lads who are already here? I’m not blaming anyone. We get it. It didn’t work. But let’s all be positive – right, it’s done, bang, let’s go. That’s what we’ve been trying to say in the dressing room.”.

Earlier this week, Mykhailo Mudryk picked up an ankle injury in training which has ruled the Chelsea loanee out of action for as long as two months.

The winger only made his debut for Tottenham as a late substitute against Nottingham Forest last week, but his attempt to rebuild his career following his anti-doping ban has been dealt a major blow.

Folarin Balogun’s proposed £39m move from Monaco collapsed on transfer deadline day, Richarlison’s return to the club didn’t materialise and Beto was sold to Fiorentina, leaving Thierno Barry as Everton’s only recognised striker.

Nottingham Forest’s pursuit of academy product Harrison Armstrong ruffled the fans’ feathers, while Iliman Ndiaye was sold to Manchester City for £60m.

Dwight McNeil, Tim Iroegbunam, Nathan Patterson, Adam Aznou and Idrissa Gueye were also allowed to leave.

Merlin Rohl and Tyrique George made their loans permanent, while Brennan Johnson, Hayden Hackney and Christian Norgaard were also added to the squad.

Summer signing Ainsley Maitland-Niles and Vitaliy Mykolenko are David Moyes’ only options at full-back.

Overall, there were a number of solid additions, just not enough of them to cover all the departures.

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of this Premier League meeting between Tottenham and Everton in the capital.

Industry observers note that are Tottenham in must-win territory already? It may seem reactionary and premature, but after spending £380m in the summer to revamp an underperforming squad, Tottenham sit inside the relegation zone, with just one point and zero goals scored in three games.

Roberto De Zerbi’s men opened the 2026-27 top-flight season with worrying back-to-back defeats to Brentford and Newcastle United, before ending their losing streak last weekend thanks to a goalless draw against Nottingham Forest.

This game gives Tottenham another opportunity to reverse their dreadful home form. Last season, Spurs managed just three league wins at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium and lost 10. The recent 2-0 loss against Newcastle was a painful reminder of Spurs’ shortcomings at home, but they’ll be expected to be authoritative and seize the initiative here today. A much-needed three points would be the perfect remedy to ease the pressure and unwanted attention on De Zerbi and his squad.

According to recent reports, meanwhile, Everton have made an unbeaten start to the season, accumulating five points from their first three league matches. David Moyes’ side looked set for defeat last time out, when they were trailing Manchester United 2-1 at the Hill Dickinson Stadium heading into stoppage time, until Ainsley Maitland-Niles’ stunning 96th-minute equaliser salvaged a draw.

Alongside drama on the pitch, there has also been noise off it. A bizarre transfer window has left Everton with a serious lack of depth up top and in both full-back positions. Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall responded to the fans’ negativity over this situation, saying their meltdowns “annoyed” him.

Nevertheless, they arrive in North London with all eyes on Tottenham and if the hosts can find a first league victory this season.

Kick-off is at 17:30, with team news coming shortly.

Il centrocampista piace a Palladino, che lo ha già allenato alla Fiorentina; Bondo è l’alternativa per gennaio.

Recent findings suggest that danilo Cataldi è il primo nome nella lista del Bologna per rinforzare il centrocampo a gennaio. Secondo quanto riportato da Corriere dello Sport, L’ipotesi dipende però da due condizioni: che il giocatore abbia superato del tutto il problema fisico con cui ha convissuto negli ultimi mesi e che le richieste di Claudio Lotito per il suo cartellino non siano troppo alte. Il contratto del centrocampista con la Lazio scade a giugno. Se la pista non dovesse concretizzarsi, l’alternativa indicata è Warren Bondo.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

il Bologna considera Cataldi una soluzione gradita e fattibile. Il club punta ad acquistare un mediano alla riapertura del mercato di gennaio, una necessità nota già da agosto.

Sources indicate that L’interesse del Bologna per Cataldi non nasce ora. Gli uomini dell’area tecnica avevano già pensato di portarlo a Casteldebole nell’anno in cui il centrocampista della Lazio passò invece alla Fiorentina. In viola trovò come allenatore Raffaele Palladino e disputò una grande stagione.

Tra il tecnico e Cataldi c’è stima reciproca. Palladino sarebbe felice di allenarlo di nuovo e anche il centrocampista ha grande considerazione di lui. Giovanni Sartori e Marco Di Vaio, per il momento, non vogliono affrontare pubblicamente il tema del mercato. La fonte ritiene possibile che si siano già mossi per capire prima le intenzioni del giocatore e poi quelle della Lazio.

Sources indicate that per il Bologna, dunque, Cataldi resta la prima scelta, a condizione che il guaio fisico sia completamente alle spalle e che l’eventuale trattativa con Lotito sia sostenibile. Il centrocampista ha 32 anni e arriverà a scadenza contrattuale a giugno.

In a recent development, se non dovessero esserci le condizioni per arrivare a Cataldi, il Bologna guarda a Warren Bondo. Il centrocampista è attualmente fuori rosa al Milan, dopo aver trascorso il campionato passato nella Cremonese. Anche lui ha già lavorato con Palladino, ai tempi del Monza.

Industry observers note that rispetto a Cataldi, Bondo è un classe 2003 e non occuperebbe un posto in lista. I due profili hanno inoltre un elemento in comune: conoscono il campionato italiano. Palladino e il Bologna cercano rinforzi che non debbano impiegare tempo per adattarsi alla realtà del calcio italiano.

Per quanto possibile, lo stesso criterio guiderà la ricerca di giocatori destinati agli altri reparti. Il discorso è più complicato soprattutto per gli attaccanti: in Italia, chi dispone di profili affidabili tende a trattenerli oppure chiede cifre che il Bologna non è disposto a spendere.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 16:26 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 16:50 EST, 23 November 2026.
  • It has been revealed that dundee manager Steven Pressley is nothing if not honest.
  • It has been revealed that you won’t hear him writing it off as a ‘bad day at the office’ or branding it a freak result from which he and his players would quickly move on.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 16:26 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 16:50 EST, 23 November 2026.

It has been revealed that dundee manager Steven Pressley is nothing if not honest. Having taken full responsibility for his team’s 8-0 thrashing by Hearts on Saturday, he now admits that the experience left him wanting to ‘crawl under a rock and hide’.

It has been revealed that you won’t hear him writing it off as a ‘bad day at the office’ or branding it a freak result from which he and his players would quickly move on. Dundee’s heaviest-ever home defeat in the league was an indignity that really hit their popular manager. And hit him hard.

In a recent development, ‘It’s been a difficult 24-48 hours,’ said Pressley. ‘There’s been a lot of hurt, a lot of embarrassment. As you can imagine, at times I’ve wanted to crawl under a rock and hide.

In a recent development, ‘It’s difficult on the back of such a disappointing result. But I will say this: I suffer a lot from vulnerability at times, but for some reason during difficult moments I seem to find strength from somewhere.

‘I don’t know if it’s from my family, from messages that I’ve received, from my reading. But I’ve had to show strength. I have to support the players. I have to make sure we navigate our way out of what was a really embarrassing moment.

‘We had a good meeting yesterday. We chatted a lot about the various aspects, and hopefully we can start responding to the disappointment.’.

Dundee boss Steven Pressley notes he felt hurt and embarrassed after losing 8-0 to Hearts.

Defender Ryan Astley struggles to take in Dundee's heaviest-ever home defeat in the league.

Recent findings suggest that that process starts tomorrow night against Hibs, who suffered a humiliation of their own when they lost 4-0 at home to Dundee United on Saturday. Pressley says the immediate objective for his team is to go there with a better attitude than they have shown lately.

Sources indicate that he had feared a setback coming for Dundee – ‘not 8-0 but a disappointing performance’ – because he had ‘sensed a little bit of subconscious complacency’. He felt his team had been over-hyped by outsiders on the back of a start to the season in which they won five of their 12 matches before the international break.

‘We’re nowhere near the levels that people keep telling us we are,’ he noted. ‘We’re not a good enough team not to do the hard yards. Our whole strength has been built on the cohesion of the team, the unity of the team, the aggressiveness of the team.

‘And I think what Saturday did highlight is exactly what I’ve been saying. If we get lazy on the hard yards, we’re a very vulnerable team. We have to be at our absolute best to get results.’.

He hopes the Hearts game will be ‘a reset moment’ that eventually helps his players to improve, but there are no guarantees from Pressley that they will shake it off at Easter Road tomorrow.

Sources indicate that asked if he expected a positive response from them, he said: ‘I don’t know. I know that they’re hurting. I know that they want to respond in the best possible way. That part I don’t question. I know how much it’s affected them.

‘But we’ve not had a lot of time. I just hope we can bring some pride back to the football club with the right type of performance.’.

The good news for Dundee is that they are up against a team who have been hopeless in their own stadium recently. Second-bottom Hibs have lost nine of their last ten Premiership games at Easter Road and haven’t taken three points there since early April.

Supporters turned on the Edinburgh side after the defeat by Dundee United, but Hibs midfielder Jamie McGrath has dismissed the idea that he and his team-mates don’t enjoy playing in their own ground.

Jamie McGrath was in the Hibs side that suffered another defeat at Easter Road on Saturday.

‘Personally, I always like playing at home,’ said McGrath. ‘I love the pitch, I love the stadium. It’s a significant open pitch, which I think should suit us. But for whatever reason, so far this season we haven’t been able to capitalise on playing at home.

‘It’s hard to put your finger on one certain thing. Maybe just being more decisive in both boxes or probably conceding goals at crucial times in the game, like after five minutes on Saturday, we just give ourselves a bit of a mountain to climb.’.

It looked like Marink Reedijk’s side had turned the corner when they followed up a rousing victory over city rivals Hearts in the Premier Sports Cup semi-final with a 4-0 win at Aberdeen in their last game before the international break.

It has been revealed that so McGrath is hoping Saturday’s aberration was a blip. ‘We’ve been on a decent run the last month and probably the international break came at a tricky time for us. We were just kind of building momentum and had two good wins back-to-back against two good teams. It’s frustrating not to build on that.’.

McGrath is unfazed by Hibs’ lowly league position and senses a chance to change that with three matches in the space of nine days against other sides in the bottom six.

Industry observers note that ‘It’s not something that we’re concerned about at the minute. It’s obviously not where we want to be. We want to try to get closer to that top six and this two-week period is quite crucial. If you put a little run together, you can boost yourself right up the league.’.

In a recent development, dans Le Patriote du Beaujolais, l'ancien gardien et capitaine caladois Franck Laurent se remémore son 16e de finale de Coupe de France perdu en aux tirs au buts contre les Verts (2-2, 1-3 tab). Extraits.

In a recent development, "Notre coach, Jean-Michel Picollet (photo), était à fond pour les Verts. C'était le derby pour nous. On était tellement contents de tomber sur eux ! Je me souviens encore de la causerie du coach, comme si c'était hier. Son message était clair et net. On allait respecter Saint-Etienne à 200% mais par contre, on allait jouer notre match à fond. Le coach nous disait qu'il y avait un truc à faire. Il nous avait mis dans cette position-là, mentalement on était prêt. On en a profité un maximum. Sur un match, on avait nos chances. On jouait sur notre terrain. Eux n'avaient pas l'habitude de ce genre de pelouse. Il y a des facteurs, dans ce genre de match, qui font que tu transcendes, que tu te mets au niveau de l'événement, tu joues ta chance à fond.

In a recent development, ce match, on en parlait tous les jours entre nous. Du début à la fin, on a vécu les choses à fond ! Ce match-là, contre Saint-Etienne, ça fait 16 ans qu'il a été joué. On m'en parle régulièrement. Pourtant, je ne suis plus du tout dans le foot. Quand on se croise, entre joueurs de cette époque, les premiers mots portent toujours sur ce match. On est liés à vie avec cette aventure de Coupe de France. C'est un petit bout de l'histoire du FCVB. J'ai eu la chance d'être là, au bon moment. Dans une carrière, ce n'est pas si évident de laisser des traces pareilles dans un club !

Recent findings suggest that les conseils que je donnerais aux Caladois d'aujourd'hui avant d'aller à Geoffroy Guichard, ce samedi ? Le contexte est totalement différent. C'est une Ligue 2 contre une Ligue 3. Il y a des joueurs professionnels des deux côtés. Je ne sais pas si je peux leur donner un conseil, à mon niveau. Mais même pour eux, ça reste des matches magnifiques à vivre. J'espère qu'ils vont arriver à s'extraire du championnat pour profiter pleinement de ce match, et tout donner. Derrière, ça peut renforcer le groupe.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.

Marathon skater Judith Krabbenborg has taken advantage of the early cold snap to smash the world one-hour record for skating on natural ice.

The 29-year-old took to the ice in Winterswijk, Gelderland, at 8.30am on Tuesday and covered a distance of 34 kilometres 878 metres, beating the previous women’s record by 2.6 kilometres.

“I could feel my legs and my back hurting at the end, but there were so many people standing on the sidelines that it gave me energy,” she told NOS.

The previous record, set four years ago by Femke Mossinkoff, also in Winterswijk, was the first official time for the hour by a woman on natural ice. On the same day Bart Vreugdenhil set the current men’s record of 36 kilometers 717 metres.

Most skating records are set on artificial ice, but Winterswijk is one of three arenas where the local club has been able to create a natural arena for early-morning skaters during the recent cold weather.

The all-time women’s record is 40 kilometres 569 metres, set by another Dutch skater, Carien Kleibeuker, in Inzell, Austria, in 2015.

The rink at Winterswijk closed a few hours after Krabbenborg’s record-breaking skate as the ice started to melt, but it is expected to be available again on Wednesday morning.

Industry observers note that ancien meneur de jeu des U17 de l'ASSE sacrés champions de France en 2013 (avec notamment Léo Pétrot, Dylan Chambost, Jonathan Bamba et Allan Saint-Maximin), le numéro 10 de Saint-Paul-en-Jarez (R3) Alexandre Assaf s'est confié au Progrès avant de défier ce dimanche Chassieu-Décines (R1) en Coupe de France. Extraits.

In a recent development, "Le président m’a proposé quelque chose d’inédit pour moi en me disant “je ne te veux pas pour mettre 40 buts par saison mais parce que j’ai beaucoup de bons jeunes qui vont monter et j’aimerais que tu les encadres, que tu les aides à se développer”. J’ai accepté direct. Je sortais de 7 saisons à Monistrol où j'ai connu 2 montées. Redescendre ce n’est pas grave, je donne plus d’importance au projet qu’au niveau.

Je parle beaucoup aux jeunes, j’essaye de les aider à passer le cap, je leur dis d’être patients quand ils jouent moins… Je suis toujours un peu décisif mais surtout content quand eux le sont. Je suis plus passeur que buteur maintenant, je préfère donner que marquer. J’ai un rôle de trentenaire, ça fait mal à dire (rires). Dimanche, en termes d’ambiance, je pense que ça va être un truc que je n’ai jamais vu. Ça va être extraordinaire.".

Industry News: Aberdeen boss Mario Frick's heavy metal football is music to the ears of their long-suffering supporters

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1256 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By CALUM CROWE, SCOTTISH DEPUTY CHIEF SPORTS WRITER.
  • Published: 16:57 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 16:57 EST, 23 November 2026.
  • As they embarked on the long journey home from Kilmarnock on Saturday night, Aberdeen supporters would surely have felt a little extra spring in their step.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CALUM CROWE, SCOTTISH DEPUTY CHIEF SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 16:57 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 16:57 EST, 23 November 2026.

As they embarked on the long journey home from Kilmarnock on Saturday night, Aberdeen supporters would surely have felt a little extra spring in their step.

If 2026 felt like it had been shaping up to be something of an annus horribilis, a 4-2 victory at Rugby Park undoubtedly lifted some of the gloom that had been hanging over the club these past few months.

According to recent reports, granted, a sample size of only one match under Mario Frick is very small. Nobody would be of a mind to get carried away with themselves just yet, especially given that Killie are easily the worst team in the league.

But there was enough in the performance, particularly during a first half which saw them score three goals in 30 minutes, to suggest that a brighter future could lie ahead under the fresh manager.

Aberdeen were aggressive, they played on the front foot, and they attacked with pace. Most of all, they were actually exciting and entertaining to watch.

Those were boxes they never ticked at any point during Stephen Robinson's time in charge. Robinson failed at Aberdeen and his team were routinely awful in terms of the quality of football they served up.

Mario Frick celebrates after a 4-2 win over Kilmarnock in his first game as Aberdeen manager.

Ante Palaversa is back in the Aberdeen team after becoming the forgotten man of Pittodrie.

Aberdeen striker Kevin Nisbet rediscovered the feelgood factor by scoring twice at Rugby Park.

In the space of only 90 minutes, Frick did more to send a wave of positivity through supporters than Robinson ever managed to do in his eight months at the helm.

The shift in mood has been as profound as it has been instantaneous, with Frick's so-called heavy metal football music to the fans' ears.

Headlines of Super Mario were always likely to follow, but Frick and his players will face an altogether tougher examination when they take on Rangers at Ibrox tomorrow.

It is an intriguing contest on various levels, with Rangers unbeaten in 13 matches as Derek McInnes goes up against his former club once again.

Given that these teams met in the Premier Sports Cup only a few weeks ago, perhaps the greatest barometer of Frick's impact will be whether Aberdeen can pose more of a threat than they did at Hampden.

It has been revealed that but what has changed? After such a turgid run of form that left players looking completely bereft of any confidence and cohesion, how was Frick able to generate an immediate improvement?

Speaking after the win at Killie, Frick was asked what sort of message he had given to the players given that time together on the training pitch had been fairly limited.

Industry observers note that 'I told them they should play like they did when they were young. In those days they didn't think about mistakes.

According to recent reports, 'They didn't think about anything negative. They played only to win, for fun.'.

Sources indicate that it was simple but refreshing. In an age of increasingly complex coaching jargon, Frick's message was intended to liberate his players – and it worked a treat.

Sources indicate that aberdeen went 2-0 up inside 12 minutes, with Kevin Nisbet scoring twice. The team looked free from the trauma of the Robinson era.

Even when Kilmarnock fought back and the game became more chaotic, Aberdeen retained enough attacking threat and collective belief to close it out.

It has been revealed that it was a huge result. A defeat would have dropped Aberdeen to the foot of the table. Instead, they climbed five places and, more importantly, rediscovered a feelgood factor.

In his previous utterances, Frick was clear that goalscoring has been the central problem.

Sources indicate that his previous teams at Vaduz and Luzern were known for their attacking output. At Luzern last season they scored 76 goals.

Sources indicate that aberdeen had managed only 12 in 12 league matches before his arrival. The early evidence suggests the players have absorbed the message promptly.

Frick's insistence on the basics – aggression, willingness to work, positive body language – appears to have cut through more effectively than more elaborate instructions might have done.

This is consistent with the picture painted by those who worked with him in Switzerland. Frick is not a rigid systems coach wedded to a single formation.

He has most often used a 4-4-2 diamond, but the shape is secondary to the mentality. High pressing to force turnovers, rapid counter-attacks, and a sense of freedom imbued to his players.

All of which makes tomorrow's clash at Ibrox all the more compelling. Aberdeen have lost their last eight meetings with Rangers in all competitions.

The previous two encounters this season, one in the Premiership and one in the Premier Sports Cup, were both settled by late Rangers goals.

The contrast in styles will be stark. Rangers are likely to control territory and force Aberdeen to defend for longer periods than they did at Rugby Park.

Frick's side will need to show that the freedom he has granted them does not dissolve into naivety when the opponent is stronger and more experienced.

The high press that worked so effectively against a struggling Killie side will have to be timed with greater precision.

According to recent reports, the attacking play will require clinical decision-making in the final third. And the defensive structure, which Frick identified as the main area for improvement after Saturday, will be examined under more sustained pressure.

Sources indicate that frick has already spoken of aiming higher than mere survival. In a league which is always extremely tight in the mid-table, top six should be the minimum target.

That may have sounded optimistic a fortnight ago. But the win at Kilmarnock suggested Aberdeen have enough about themselves to be looking up rather than over their shoulders.

The squad still needs greater consistency and, in certain areas, greater quality.

But there is already evidence to suggest he can get a tune out of some players who either under-performed under Robinson or, in some cases, those who had been totally discarded.

Ante Palaversa would surely be chief among them. The Croatian midfielder hardly kicked a ball under Robinson and had become the forgotten man at Pittodrie.

Brought in to make his first league start of the season, his performance at Killie and the way he controlled things in midfield made his exclusion under Robinson look all the more bizarre.

None of this is to say that Aberdeen are suddenly a top-class football team. At best, they remain very much a work in progress.

Yet, crucially, Frick immediately has the supporters onboard in a way that Robinson never managed to do.

Frick and his players could yet be given a major reality check if they were to suffer a hefty defeat to a Rangers side unbeaten in 13 matches.

It has been revealed that but there is belief and positivity in the camp at Pittodrie. Feelgood factors in football can often be fragile and often short-lived, but they are also real.

When players begin to play with freedom and confidence, results usually tend to take care of themselves.

Sources indicate that frick has not yet transformed Aberdeen. He has, however, given the players and the fans a reason to believe that a brighter future could lie ahead.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that né à Saint-Priest-en-Jarez et formé à L’Étrat dès l'âge de 8 ans, Maedine Makhloufi avait signé son premier contrat professionnel avec les Verts en mai 2025 avant de mettre le cap sur Dunkerque l'hiver dernier. Tout juste prêté au FC Villefranche Beaujolais (Ligue 3), le latéral gauche de 21 ans s'apprête à retrouver Geoffroy-Guichard dès ce samedi (19h) à l'occasion du 8e tour de la Coupe de France. Avant ces retrouvailles au goût forcément particulier, l'ancien protégé du centre de formation s'est confié en toute simplicité à Poteaux Carrés.

Maedine, tu es né à deux pas de L'Étrat, à Saint-Priest-en-Jarez, et tu as poussé les portes de l’ASSE à seulement 8 ans. Quel est ton premier souvenir de gamin en Vert ?

Mon tout premier souvenir, c'est lors de ma détection. J'arrivais de l'Olympique du Montcel, à La Ricamarie. On avait raté les détections pour la génération 2005, donc je les ai passées avec les 2006. À la fin, ils m'ont demandé si j'étais né en 2006, je leur ai répondu que j'étais de 2005 et ils m'ont dit de revenir le lendemain avec ma génération. Tout est parti de là. C’est un cousin qui m’avait emmené ce jour-là, il m'avait dit : « Tu vas venir t'entraîner ». À 8 ans, tu ne réalises pas vraiment où tu mets les pieds, j'étais juste venu jouer au foot et m'amuser.

Le foot, c'était déjà toute ta vie à cet âge-là ?

According to recent reports, oui, depuis tout petit. J'avais toujours un ballon avec moi, dès que je pouvais. En bas de chez moi, il y avait un stade, donc on passait notre temps là-bas avec mon grand frère, mes nombreux cousins et les potes du quartier.

Durant tes douze années au centre, y a-t-il un éducateur qui t'a plus marqué que les autres ?

Recent findings suggest that franchement, je n'en ai pas un en particulier qui ressort. Je n'ai croisé que de bonnes personnes, on a vraiment été très bien entourés, ils ont tous été magnifiques. Quand je suis arrivé à l'école de foot, on s'entraînait encore au stade à Méons, juste à côté de Geoffroy-Guichard. Puis en U12, on a basculé au centre de formation à L’Étrat, c'est devenu plus carré, plus cadré. Il y a eu des saisons plus compliquées que d'autres, mais j'ai franchi toutes les étapes jusqu'à la réserve et mon premier contrat pro. Je n'en garde que du positif.

Quels sont tes souvenirs les plus forts de toutes ces années de formation ?

Sources indicate that les derbies contre l'Olympique Lyonnais, sans hésiter ! Chaque week-end de derby, même quand on était tout petits, c'était magnifique, toute la semaine était spéciale. Et puis tous les tournois, les moments de vie entre coéquipiers, ce ne sont que des super souvenirs.

Le 28 mai 2025, tu signes ton premier contrat professionnel avec ton club formateur. Qu'est-ce qui se passe dans la tête d'un enfant du Forez à ce moment-là ?

It has been revealed that C'est la récompense de tout le travail accompli. Avant tout, une immense fierté, pour moi mais surtout pour mes proches. On n'a pas fait de grosse fête particulière, mais tout le monde était heureux et j'ai senti que j'avais rendu ma famille fière.

In a recent development, tu n'as pas paraphé ce contrat tout seul puisque Jules Mouton a signé le sien le même jour que toi. Vous vous êtes un peu chambrés ?

Non, parce qu'on le savait un petit peu avant. Jules est arrivé un an après moi, on a fait pratiquement tout notre parcours ensemble, donc arriver là main dans la main, c'était magnifique. On est restés très proches. Je garde d'ailleurs le contact avec la plupart des gars de la génération 2005 sur les réseaux. Avec Jules, on s'est même croisés en Ligue 2 cette saison puisqu'il joue à Grenoble, on a un peu rigolé avant le match.

Qu'est-ce qui a motivé ton départ vers Dunkerque au mercato d'hiver dernier ?

In a recent development, J'ai reçu un appel de Dunkerque et ça s'est fait très vite. À Saint-Étienne, je n'avais pas beaucoup de temps de jeu : je jouais en réserve mais pas du tout avec l'équipe première. C'était une belle opportunité pour moi, les deux clubs se sont mis d'accord sans aucun problème.

Après douze ans dans le cocon stéphanois, comment s'est passée ton intégration dans le Nord ?

According to recent reports, super bien, franchement nickel. À Saint-Étienne, je m'étais déjà pas mal entraîné avec le groupe pro, donc rien qu'en observant les anciens, tu apprends vite. Et à Dunkerque, le groupe était jeune avec que des bons mecs. Bon, comme on est tout près de la mer, il y a souvent du vent, mais on s'y fait (rires) !

It has been revealed that là-bas, tu as choisi de porter le numéro 42. C'était un message subliminal pour dire que la Loire ne te quittait jamais ?

(Rires) Oui, c'était clairement un clin d'œil ! Comme je suis arrivé en cours de saison, il ne restait plus énormément de numéros libres et j'ai tout de suite sauté sur le 42. J'ai reçu plein de messages sympas de supporters stéphanois grâce à ça, et même dans le Nord, tout le monde savait à quoi ça correspondait !

According to recent reports, même si tu aurais aimé jouer davantage, tu as quand même eu le temps de marquer un but express en 4 minutes dans un derby face à Boulogne ! Qu'as-tu appris chez les Maritimes ?

C'était une sensation incroyable, mon premier but chez les pros et dans un derby en plus, tu ne peux pas rêver mieux ! Ces mois à Dunkerque m'ont fait basculer du monde semi-pro au monde pro. J'ai énormément appris sur les détails tactiques, l'exigence de concentration et l'impact physique. La réserve en N3 te prépare bien parce que tu affrontes des adultes, mais l'étage au-dessus, c'est encore un autre monde.

Tu viens tout juste de poser tes valises au FC Villefranche Beaujolais en prêt pour retrouver du rythme en Ligue 3. Passer de la mer du Nord aux vignes du Beaujolais, le choc climatique et gastronomique n'est pas trop rude ?

Recent findings suggest that (Rires) Non, franchement ça va très bien ! En plus, je me rapproche de la maison. Et puis dans le Beaujolais, on mange bien et on boit bien aussi, donc l'adaptation est facile.

Sources indicate that tu es arrivé lundi dernier à Villefranche, et le tirage au sort t'envoie directement dans le Chaudron ce samedi ! Tu as vérifié que la FFF n'avait pas truqué les boules juste pour ton histoire personnelle ?

C'est possible ça (rires) ! Non, plus sérieusement, c'est un scénario magnifique. J'ai déjà eu la chance de rejouer 5 ou 10 minutes à Geoffroy-Guichard avec Dunkerque la saison dernière, et revenir chez moi devant ma famille et mes amis, c'était quelque chose de fort. Ce samedi, mes proches seront encore en tribunes. Maintenant, je ne suis pas le coach, j'espère avant tout être dans le groupe et avoir du temps de jeu.

Pour les supporters stéphanois qui t'ont un peu perdu de vue, quel joueur es-tu devenu aujourd'hui dans ton couloir gauche ?

In a recent development, J'ai beaucoup travaillé sur mes défauts depuis mon départ à Dunkerque, on avait ciblé certains points précis et je me suis accroché. J'ai gagné en expérience et en maturité, dans mon jeu comme en dehors. Aujourd'hui, je suis un joueur plus complet et plus fort.

Qu'est-ce qui te motive au quotidien quand tu te lèves pour aller à l'entraînement ?

Industry observers note that je me dis simplement que j'ai l'un des plus beaux métiers du monde ! Il y a plein de gens qui se lèvent tôt pour faire des boulots bien plus difficiles que le nôtre, donc on n'a vraiment pas le droit de se plaindre. Même s'il y a toujours des séances plus dures que d'autres, je vais à l'entraînement avec le sourire. Le jour où je ne prendrai plus de plaisir, j'arrêterai.

Parmi les jeunes du centre qui sont aujourd'hui dans le groupe pro stéphanois, lequel redoutes-tu le plus d'affronter samedi soir ?

Ils ont tous beaucoup de qualités, mais je pense forcément à Kevin Pedro. On a un an d'écart, on a énormément joué ensemble et on était très proches. Il fait une saison magnifique et ça ne m'étonne pas du tout : il a toujours été très fort et joue avec beaucoup d'intelligence. Tout ce qui lui arrive est amplement mérité.

Dernière question : imaginons qu'on joue la 89e minute samedi, qu'il y a toujours 0-0 et que tu te retrouves seul face au gardien vert. Tu vises la lucarne pour qualifier Villefranche ou tu rends hommage à notre site en frappant volontairement sur le poteau carré — même s'ils sont ronds aujourd'hui ?

(Éclat de rire) Je pense que je vais plutôt viser le filet ! Tant pis pour Poteaux Carrés.

Industry observers note that un grand merci à toi Maedine pour ta disponibilité. Toute l'équipe de Poteaux Carrés te souhaite le meilleur pour la suite et de pouvoir fouler la pelouse samedi… sans marquer si possible !

Merci beaucoup à vous ! Quel que soit le résultat, ce sera une belle fête. Sur un match de Coupe, l'écart entre une Ligue 2 et une Ligue 3 n'est pas si grand, tout reste possible.

Bruno Guimarães cupped his ears and had a plastic cup thrown at him as the abuse came down from the stands. Despite the missiles, the Brazilian wore a look that made it clear he was very much enjoying his first goal in an Arsenal shirt.

Mikel Arteta has laid bare his quirky management techniques so his players are ready for any eventuality. Late meals and making the dressing room hotter are among his tricks, although nothing can prepare a player having 40,000 fans calling you a “sad Geordie b------”.

According to recent reports, so it was a sweet moment for Guimarães, even more so after coming just after Sunderland had a penalty saved. Just 121 seconds after Enzo Le Fée had his spot kick tipped on to a post by David Raya, Guimarães was rubbing salt into the wound with a stunning long-range strike that went in off the crossbar.

It has been revealed that the former Newcastle captain gave the perfect response after being taunted his old rivals. “It was a beautiful goal,” he noted. “Everyone knows my past, I had an amazing history at Newcastle. But now I’m trying to create a newly introduced history here and I have started on the right foot.”.

What an vital week it has been for Arsenal, who have shown their squad depth by winning in Napoli then travelling to the Stadium of Light and extending their perfect start to the season to six games.

Other teams with aspirations of the title dropped points earlier in the day, while Arteta could battle to a win with key players brought back into the team and Guimarães coming off the bench at half-time. A trip in the Champions League followed by an away game the following weekend is a barometer of where teams are, and Arsenal have sounded a warning after coming through a bruising encounter.

Régis Le Bris’s team offer a challenge that is impossible to replicate, even by the standards of Arteta’s “sabotage” to make his players uncomfortable. Fans belted out Elvis Presley and 90s anthem Ready To Go just before kick-off. Then there was the aggression that Arsenal players faced. There were complaints of elbows being aimed at Gabriel Magalhães.

Bukayo Saka scored a stoppage-time penalty to seal the win but the evening belonged to Guimarães, the £75m summer signing who has been waiting for this moment to ignite his Arsenal career.

Recent findings suggest that “Everyone knows I had a difficult start through injuries in my short time. But I’m glad to be back and glad to play,” Guimarães remarked. “I feel very good. It was unbelievable to score a beautiful goal, beautiful moment for me and my family and I am happy.”.

Recent findings suggest that these are ominous signs for Arsenal’s title rivals, with Guimarães’s return to fitness adding to the midfield options. Arteta’s changes to his starting line-up restored Riccardo Calafiori and Kai Havertz – two of the in-form players in the Premier League – to the team, rather than squad players being rotated.

And his players stood up to a physical challenge. Brian Brobbey used his frame to back into the Arsenal’s centre-backs, who are unlikely to given such a tough assignment this season aside from facing Erling Haaland.

Recent findings suggest that guimarães was brought on at half-time along with Jurriën Timber, which was another sign of Arsenal mounting a strong defence of their title. With Arteta’s changes altering the pace of the game, the match turned just before the hour mark. John Brooks saw nothing in the incident that floored Gabriel at a corner, but at the next set-piece penalised Ezri Konsa for wrestling with Dan Ballard, much to Arteta’s fury.

Le Fée had earned a point against Brentford a week earlier with a penalty, but this time his finish was tipped on to the post by David Raya. “We should not talk about the save of the keeper, we should talk about what happened before that,” added Arteta.

“But I loved the save from David, the way the team reacted, the way we go again and we go against everything, but this should never happen, it’s not fair, and I am sad, very sad, in that sense.”.

Recent findings suggest that raya also denied Nordi Mukiele from close range when Granit Xhaka’s expertly taken free-kick found his team-mate in front of goal. Sunderland have their own European campaign starting on Thursday and will start with confidence after pushing the champions all the way.

Brooks awarded a penalty in stoppage-time when Saka was brought down by Reinildo Mandava, who was dismissed. “I’m extremely pleased to win again. We had a really tough week, Chelsea, Napoli, winning there and now against a really tough opponent in a difficult place,” added Arteta.

Mikel Arteta rolled out a furious attack on referee John Brooks for awarding a penalty against Arsenal and fears similar decisions will cost his team the Premier League title.

Brooks gave a spot-kick for Ezri Konsa tussling with Dan Ballard, although Arteta accused the Sunderland centre-back of a “judo roll”.

Enzo Le Fée’s penalty was saved by David Raya, with Arsenal winning after goals from Bruno Guimarães and Bukayo Saka.

Industry observers note that “I’m sad that we have to discuss something in such a beautiful game at this level. That has gravity because that changes the course of the season and it can cost you the championship. And at this level, with all the work that we put in, this cannot happen.

“You see, it is a judo roll and it brings the player on the floor. So how can this happen? I cannot find an explanation. That’s why I’m trying to find that.”.

The win rounded off a positive week for Arsenal despite Arteta’s fury at the officials.

Sources indicate that “I’m extremely pleased to win again. We had a really tough week, Chelsea, Napoli, winning there and now against a really tough opponent in a difficult place. Sources indicate that “I’m making it very clear publicly because it’s for the game, it’s not only for Arsenal, this cannot happen at this level. We should not talk about the save of the keeper, we should talk about what happened before that.”.

Sources indicate that guimarães’s goal was his first for Arsenal, with Arteta adding: “Beautiful, he came on, the goal, the assist, remarkable. That why we talk about the finishers and making that impact and being able to support and help the team. He was outstanding.”.

Three points or not, the Arsenal manager is furious about the penalty that was awarded to Sunderland.

In the thick Naples air in midweek, Declan Rice did what he always does: he kept running. Another start for the Arsenal midfielder, another 90 minutes completed and another performance of constructive passing and destructive defending. For anyone who was worried about Rice’s physical condition, it was an emphatic response.

Recent findings suggest that after that Champions League victory over Napoli, Rice insisted he was ready for another marathon campaign. He made 69 appearances for club and country last season, up from 60 the previous term, and believes that is a sustainable number of games, even for an all-action midfielder such as himself. “I have shown I can do it,” he said.

The key question, though, is not whether Rice can do it, but whether he should do it. There is no doubt that his body eventually began to pay the price for his exertions last year, especially during the World Cup, and it would be reasonable for his managers to worry that his extraordinary workload might one day take a serious toll. This, after all, is a footballer who managed nerve pain in his hamstring throughout the second half of last season.

Sunderland are the latest team tasked with stopping Arsenal, who have begun their title defence in formidable style: they’ve won out of three, including a dominant comeback victory against Chelsea last weekend, and look well equipped to become the first Arsenal team to retain the title since the mid-1930s.

According to recent reports, there’s a long way to go, and Arsenal fans will remember how blisteringly they started their last two title defences in 2002-03 and 2004-05, only to ultimately fall short. But right now, they could barely be in better shape. Their fine start to the season came with a Champions League win in Naples, achieved despite a delay to their flight from London.

“I love those challenges,” stated Mikel Arteta. “I try to create them in pre-seasons so when they happen, we already experience them and we already know. So get to the stadium very late, change the routine and suddenly the players have to do something else.

Recent findings suggest that “Because when it happens, and it can happen, you can miss the flight, the train can be delayed, there’s so much traffic and I don’t want the players, but not only the players, the staff as well, panicking. So when that happens, adapt to it.”.

Sources indicate that arteta has tested his squad in a variety of ways. “[We have] delayed the meals, delayed the transport, taken a different route. We’ve done many things – made the dressing room hotter, more difficult, more challenging, less beds... because we’re going to have to adapt to different contexts.”.

So far, they’re adapting very well to the context of being the reigning champions.

PSV and Feyenoord face an uphill task to reach the group stages of the Champions League after defeats on Tuesday night saw them drop out of the qualifying places.

PSV briefly threatened to cause an upset in Madrid as they took a 1-0 lead into the half-time break. Ivan Perisic’s penalty after 32 minutes was their only reward for a courageous first-half display in which Ruben van Bommel and Sven Mijnans also missed clear chances to score.

But the introduction of Jude Bellingham at half-time changed the picture as Real’s superstars regrouped to score five goals. The England midfielder’s dazzling volley was the pick of the bunch, while Kylian Mbappé bagged a double and Vinicius Junior also got on the scoresheet.

It has been revealed that head coach Peter Bosz admitted his team had been “trampled underfoot” in the second half. “I think you had to be there to see how big the difference was between the first and second half,” he remarked.

“In the first half we were brave, put our opponents under pressure and had three major chances in the first four minutes.

“When you look at the second half, they scored quickly and the tempo of their game was much higher. That’s the quality they have with the players they can bring off the bench.”.

PSV’s next match is a home tie against Real’s city rivals Atletico on December 9, before they travel to Stavanger to take on Viking in January and round off the group stage at home to Stuttgart.

Feyenoord suffered a narrower defeat at home to Porto as they were unable to recover from an own goal after two minutes by Oussama Targhalline.

Goalkeeper Florian Kastenmeier vindicated the decision of Giovanni van Bronckhorst to replace the out-of-form Tjark Ernst by making some vital saves to keep the Rotterdammers in the game.

Feyenoord staged a late rally, with Gjivai Zechiël going close and Targhalline striking the crossbar from long range, but they were unable to breach the Portuguese side’s defence.

The fans in De Kuip were briefly celebrating after a bizarre incident when referee Irfan Peltjo’s watch told him a header by Nacho Ferri had crossed the line, but video replays clearly indicated it bounced off the post and into the hands of Diogo Costa.

According to recent reports, feyenoord have just three points from their five matches so far, one less than PSV. Their next two matches are away to Viking on December 8 and Galatasaray on January 19, before they close their campaign in Rotterdam against RB Leipzig.
